AWARD 


The Government of West Bengal, Labour Depart- 
ment, by order No. 1046-I.R./IR/11L-160/67, dated 
23rd February 1968, referred under section 10 of the 
Industrial Disputes Act to this Tribunal an industrial 
dispute existing between Messrs. Sen Raleigh Ltd., 
Kanyapuf, P.O. Asansol and their workmen represent- 
ed by Sen Raleigh Cycle Factory Mazdoor Congress, 
Kanyapur, P.O. Ethora, Asansol, for adjudication in 
respect of the following issue : 


Issue 


Is the dismissal of Shri Sarju Prasad, T. No. 1396, 
with effect from 7th October 1967 justified? 
‘I'o what relief, in any, is he entitled? 


On behalf of the Union Shri Samar Roy, Assistant 
Secretary, appeared and the Company was represented 
by Advocate Shri J..N. Chatterjee. The ‘Union did 
neither examine any witness’ nor produce any docu- 
ment. ‘fie Company examined two witnesses O.P.W. 1 


eed 
eee = Lee - ee 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, JANUARY 16, 1969 69 


SS AS EE 
omar 


Shri B. N. Bagchi, Personnel Officer and O.P.W. 2 
Shri 5. C. Sen, Technical Assistant in the Hubs Depart- 
ment. 9011) the witnesses were cross-examined ৪1 
length by the learned representative for the Union. 


The case of the Union in the written statement, inter 
alia, is that the workmen of the Company were organi- 
sed under two Unions—one dominated by the ۸۴۰ 
Party and the other ‘Sen Raleigh Cycle Factory 
Mazdoor Congress" affiliated to INTUC. Thé Com- 
pany have* had some secret arrangement with the 
former Union and rcognises the same, while the bona 
fide Trade Union activities of the latter Union is 
opposed by it. Some leaders of this Union affiliated 
with the INTUC were forced to leave the services of 
the Company. Shri Sarju Prosad, T. No. 1396, is 
another leader of this Union and he was dismissed on 
false and flimsy pretext. He was served with a charge- 
sheet, dated 22nd July 1967, containing a false and 
malicious charge which was denied by him in_ his 
explanation in reply to the charge-sheet. The Com- 
pany thereafter held a perfunctory enquiry and 
managed to dismiss this workman in order to get rid 
of him for his trade union activitics. The enquiry 
was held in violation of the principles of natural 
justice. 


The case of the Company in brief is that Shri Sarju 
Prosad was working since 12th May 1958 and he was 
dismissed for acts of gross misconduct. On 2151 July 
1967 at about 9-20 a.m. while this workman was 
uperating Machine No. H-3, he was found by the 
Technical Assistant of the Department rotating 
manually the figure-index of the piece counting gadget 
of the Press Machine without operating the said Press 
Machine with a clear motive to inflate his production 
ligure for wrongful gains and accordingly 176 was, 
charge: sheeted for committing acts of gross miscon- 
duct. Tne Company offered him all opportunities to 
defend himself against the charges by examining his 
own winesses and by cross-examining the witnesses 
deposing against him in the domestic enquiry held on 
26th July 1967, As he was found guilty 11 the 
enquiry he was dismissed by letter, dated 7th October 
1967. The Company denies the allegation of victi- 
misation as revealed by the Union. 


O.P.W. ] Shri B. N. Bagchi, Personnel Officer, 
says that he held the enquiry on the  charge-sheet 
issued against Sarju Prasad. Ext. A is the charge- 
sheet, dated 22nd July 1967. It is alleged that on 21st 
July 1967, at above 9.20 a.m., Shri S. C. Sen, Techni- 
cal Assistant found this workman rotating manually 
the figure index of the Piece Counting Gadget with a 
view to inflate his production figure for wrongful 
gains. This Technical Assistant in the Hubs Depart- 
ment, viz.. O.P.W. 2, Shri S. C. Sen, states in his evi- 
dence in this Tribunal that Sarju Prosad was a Press 
Operator in the Hubs Department where production 
in the machine is recorded by Piece Counting Gadget. 
The Operator operates the machine by pressing hand 
lever and by each stroke of the machine the Gadget 
mechanically indicates an increase by one number. The 
material produced is kept in a bin and from that bin it 
goes to the next machine for further operation. An 
Operator would not necessarily start his production with 
an empty bin always inasmuch as the bin in which his 
production is being put in would contain the production 
of the previous Operators. A bin ٭اٴ‎ replaced only 
when it is filled up. As the production process goes on, 
subsequent operations are fed from these bins. The 


70 THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, JANUARY 16, 1969: 


০ সপ সু 


Operator may increase the figure in the Gadget by put- 
ting his finger in the Gadget after rotating the wheel 
without operating the machine ; but the number cannot 
be decreased by such operation as the Gadget moves 
only in clock-wise direction when the figures are increa- 
ed and it cannot be moved anti-clock-wise. When the 
production made by a particular workman is finished 
the figures in the Gadget are brought to zero by a 
special key which is kept in the office and the shift 
Supervisor is responsible tu use this key to bring down 
the figure. As the materials produced cannot be coun- 
ted by any means, these figures go to the accounts for 
making payment to the workman concerned according 
to his individual production. 


From this evidence of O.P.W. 2, Shri S. C. Sen, it 
appears that an Operator may increase the figure 
showing his production by rotating the Gadget manual- 
ly without operating the machine. Of course, this will 
be tantamount to wrongful gain as the Company makes 
payment according to the figures shown in the Gadget. 
In the charge-shect Sarju Prosad was directed to show 
cause and his explanation appears in the reverse of the 
charge-sheet, viz., Ext. B. He has denied the allegations 
totally. Ext. C is the order of the General Manager 
showing that the explanation submitted by Sarju Prosad 
was not found satisfactory and Shri B. N. Bagchi was 
appointed as Enquiry Ofticer by this order. Ext. D, 
dated 24th July 1967, is the notice of enquiry showing 
that the enquiry would be held on 26th July 1967. 
Ext. E is the proceedings of the enquiry. From the 
record of the proceedings and the evidence of Shri 
Bagchi (O.P.W. 1) it appears that the charge-sheeted 
workman Sarju Prosad was present all along with a co- 
worker Shri Mahatam Singh. ‘The charge-sheet and 
the explanation were read over and explained to the 
delinquent and it was made clear to him that he would 
be allowed opportunity to defend his case and to adduce 
evidence, if any, and also cross-examine the witnesses of 
the prosecution. The Company produced the com- 
plainant and three witnesses and Sarju Prosad declined 
to produce any witness. The Enquiry Officer recorded 
the statements of the witnesses of the prosecution 
in answer to questions put by him and Sarju Prosad 
and his observer were asked to cross-examine each 
witness. It appears that Sarju Prosad actually cross- 
examined all the four witnesses of the prosecution and 
the statements made in cross-examination of these wit- 
nesses were duly recorded by Shri Bagchi. Shri Bagchi 
says that he put questions to the witnesses of the 
management in Bengali and answers given by them 
were recorded in Bengali and he explained the questions 
and the answers in Hindi language before Sarju Prosad 
cross-examined these witnesses. The questions put by 
Sarju Prosad to the witnesses were recorded in Hindi 
language, though in Bengali script, and the answers 
given by the witnesses were similarly recorded. The 
witnesses for the management and also Sarju Prosad 
and his observer all put their signatures in each page 
of the proceedings. 


From the evidence it is abundantly clear that all the 
principles of natural justice were duly observed. The 
finding Ext. F shows that the Enquiry Officer consider- 
ed the evidence carefully and this finding is neither 
without basis nor perverse. Under the law an Indus- 
trial Tribunal will not ordinarily substitute its own 
judgment to that of the domestic Tribunal, and it can 
interfere only the following grounds :— 


(1) when there is a want of good faith, 


[PART IC 

সি 

(2) when there is victimisation or unfair labour 
practice, ° 


been guilty of a 
principle of 


(3) when the management has 
basis error or yiolation of a 
natural justice, and 


(4) when on the materials the finding is completely 
baseless or perverse. 


I have already shown that all the principles of natu- 
ral justice were duly observed and the finding is not 
baseless or perverse. As regards victimisation though 
there is such an allegation in the written statement, the 
workman has not given any evidence in support of this 
allegation. He has neither deposed himself nor exa- 
mined any witness. In the absence of any evidence I 
am unable to hold that the management dismissed Sarju 
Prosad to victimise him for his Union activities as 
alleged. 


Apart from the enquiry proceeding the case of the 
Company is also proved in this Tribunal by O.P.W. 2, 
S. C. Sen, the Technical Assistant of the Hubs Depart- 
ment. He says that he actually found Sarju Prosad 
rotating the Gadget manually and before him he ad- 
mitted that he had in fact increased the number of 
production by 50 figures by such manual operation. 
The learned representative of the Union has taken ob- 
jection as the Company has not examined any other 
workman of this department to prove this allegation 
against Sarju Prosad, but the evidence of Shri Sen 
goes unchallenged. Neither Sarju  Prosad nor any 
other workman is coming to deny this statement. 1ا‎ 
hold that the Enquiry Officer rightly found Sarju 
Prosad guilty of the charge and the management was 
justified to dismiss him upon this charge. Ext. G is the 
note given by the Personnel Manager to the General 
Manager recommending dismissal of Sarju Prosad and 
the order of the General Manager is Ext. G(1). The 
dismissal order was communicated to the workman by 
letter Ext. H, dated 7th October 1967, and he was 
asked to collect his dues, if any. 


It was argued by the learned representative for the 
workman that under the Standing Orders the manage- 
ment can suspend a workman for seven days only 
pending enquiry into the charge-sheet against him ; but 
in the instant case Shri Prosad was under suspension 
throughout the period till his dismissal. It' was con- 
tended by the learned Advocate for the Company that 
when the offence is established the suspension beyond 
the prescribed period will not exonerate the workman. 
There -is substance in this contention. Sarju Prosad 
should be deemed to be in service for the entire period 
till his dismissal barring the first seven days of suspen. 
sion pending enquiry on the charge. So he ig entitled 
to his wages for this period. It is the evidence of 
O.P.W. 1, Shri Bagchi, that Sarju Prosad was paid all 
his dues for the entire period of suspension barring 
first seven days till his dismissal. The learned repre- 
sentative of the Union submits that the Company has 
not paid the entire dues to Sarju Prosad and accord- 
ing to him his total dues would be Rs. 537.65P, 
whereas the Company paid only Ks. 350.00. But 
there is no such allegation in the pleading nor is there 
any evidence to prove this claim. 


Considering all these facts and circumstances and 
the evidence in record 1 find that dismissal of Sarju 
Prosad, T. No. 1396, with effect from 7th October

1907, is justifed. If any amount be found due to him 
the Company should pay the same to him within one 
month from the date of publication of this award in 
the Official Gazette. 


This is my award. 


Dictated and corrected by me.

No. 1, has heen examined as the sole witness on behalf 
of the Union. Several documents were produced and 
exhibited in this case. P.W. 1 and the exhibited docu- 
ments prove that the alleged domestic enquiries against 
the five workmen mentioned in Issue No. 1 of 016 
order of reference, are vitiated by the principles of 
natural justice. P.W. 1 has also proved that there was 
victimisation and unfair labour practice in this case 
in the matter of dismissing the said five workmen. 
Accordingly, I hold that the dismissal of the following 
_ workmen by the Company with effect from Ath Septem- 
ber 1967 (vide Ext. 5 series—the letters of dismissal) 
is not at all justified. P.W. 1 in his evidence has also 
said that the management was not at all justified in 
laying off the 59 workmen mentioned in the list 
attached to the order of reference from 7th May 1966 
to 18th May 1966. I accept the evidence of P.W. | 
as correct and I hold that the management is not al 
all justified in laying off the 59 workmen mentioned in 
the list attached to the order of reference from 7th 
May 1966 to 18th May 1966. I further hold that the 
said 59 workmen are entitled to their full wages during 
this period, their wages during the relevant time 
having been mentioned against their names in the list 
attached to the order of reference. Accepting the 
evidence of P.W. 1, I also hold that the management 
is not at all justified in refusing employment to all the 
59 workmen mentioned in the list attached to the order 
of reference, referred to above, on and from 20th 
June 1966. It is the evidence of P.W. 1 that the 
factory is still in running condition. Accordingly | 
further hold that the said 59 workmen are entitled to 
reinstatement. As P.W. 1 in his evidence simply prayed 
for order of reinstatement and as he has not prayed 
for back wages, I hold that the five workmen as men- 
tioned under Jssue No. 1 and the 59 workmen as men- 
tioned in the list attached to the order of reference are 
only entitled to order of reinstatement. The said 59 
workmen are further entitled to full wages on and from 
“th May 1966, till 18th May 1966, their wages having 
been mentioned against their names in the list attached 
tu the order of reference, and I hold as such. 


The Company is directed to reinstate the five work- 
men Shri Amulya Hazra, Shri Basanta Lal Das, Shri 
Narain Dey, Shri Ram Prakash and Shri Mahadev Das 
and also 59 workmen as mentioned in the list attached 
to the order of reference within one month from the 
date of publication of this award in the “Calcutta 
Gazette.” 


The Company is further directed to pay the full 
wages to the said 59 workmen in the list attached to 
the order of reference for the period from 7th May 
1966 till 18th May 1966 after deducting any amount. 
if already paid on any occasion for this period, from 
7th May 1966 till 18th May 1966 also, within one 
month from the date of publication of this award in 
the “Calcutta Gazette”. 


This is my award.

Usual notices were served from this Tribunal, 
after receipt of the Order of Reference, to the 
Union as well as the Company. Both the Com- 
pany as well as the Union appeared and file. 
their separate written statements. 


The Union in its written statement contended 
that the Company being Messrs. Shree Govinda 
Aluminium Works is one of the prosperous units 
of the industry and by manufacturing aluminium 
sheets, circles, strips and electrical components, 
is earning huge profits 6৬61৬ year. The em- 
ployees being  piece-rated workers, their earnings 
depended on production. The Company in order 
to increase their profits and to exploit the lab- 
ourers started supplying bad and inferior types 
of materials and as such the earnings of the 
labourers fell abnormally. The workers approa- 
ched the Management to ventilate their gricvan- 
ces for inferior types of materials many a times 
and at Jast the Director told the workers to put 
their grievances in writing. Accordingly on the 
23rd July 1966 they placed their grievances in 
writing by submitting an application (vide Ext. 
1), but the Company authorities did not redress 
the grievances of the labourers and at last, the 
Union approached the Labour Commissioner by 
way of submission of their demands by a letter, 
dated the 10th August 1966 (vide Ext. ‘A’). On 
fetting such letter of the Union, the Management 
got very much annoyed. On 8th October 1966, 
all the workers went and resumed their work 
as usual. After sometime, about 15 workmen 
met the Director to place their grievances and 
in turn the Director turned them out of the fac- 
tory and these 15 workmen were not allowed 
to resume their work. The Management by a 
letter, dated 12th August 1966 (vide Ext. ‘B’), 
made false allegations to the effect that 11716 
workers were not resuming their work. In 
order to terrorise the workmen, the Company 
actually refused to give work to the 15 work- 
men mentioned in the Order of Reference on the 
plea that they had left their job voluntarily and 
issued letters on 19th August 1966 (vide Ext. 'D’) 
stating that they had struck off their names from 
the master roll of the Company.: The Company 
before issuing the letter, dated 19th August 1966 
(vide Ext. ‘D’), did not comply with the forma- 
lities of law which are required, before dismiss- 
ing a person, which is a clear instance of unfair 
labour practice. The action taken by the Com- 
pany is unjustified, mala fide and by way of

Exts. ‘P’ and also P-1). The Lease in favour of

the Company's case. 


Upon a consideration of the entire evidence on 
record, both oral and documentary, and the facts as 
well as the circumstances of this case ৪৪ stated 
above, I cannot but accept the Company's conten- 
tion to the effect that the workers mentioned in the 
Order of Reference went on strike from during the 
tiffin time of 8th August 1966, as true. Accord- 
ingly I hold that the employees of the Spinning 
Department of Shree Govinda Aluminium Works 
actually struck work from the noon time of 8th 
August 1966, which is the Company’s case. I thus 
hold that there was no refusal of employment to 
any of the following workmen as mentioned 10) the 
Order of Reference as alleged on behalf of the 
Union. So the question of justification of alleged 
refusal of employment to the workmen does nat 
crise in this case and as such ] hold that none of 
the employees are entitled to any relief in this Order 
of Reference. 


Next, as regards the contention raised on behalf 
of the Company that the instant Order of Reference 
is not maintainable, because prior to this Order of 
Reference, there was never any placement or raising 
cf the alleged dispute regarding refusal of employ- 
ment to any of the employees before the Company 
authorities, | may mention here that this contention 
has got some force. There is nothing on record to 
show that the workmen raised any dispute with their 
employers regarding the alleged refusal of employ- 
ment to the workmen as mentioned in the Order of 
Reference. A mere demand to the Government with- 
out a dispute being raised by the workmen with their 
employers cannot become an industrial dispute. In 
the instant case, the Government had to come to an 
opinion that an industrial dispute did exist and that 
opinion could ‘only be formed on the basis that there 
was a dispute between the Company and the Union 
relating to refusal of employment and relating to 
reinstatement. The only reference that the Govern- 
ment could have made, had to be related to the 
payment of retrenchment compensation which could 
be the only subject-matter of dispute. ۱ 

As the Order of Reference stands, ] answer the 
first part of the issue in the affirmative and the second 
part in the negative. This Order of Reference, | 
hold, is not maintainable either on facts or on law. 


This is my award.

In the matter of an industrial dispute existing 
between Messrs. Himant Private Ltd., 13 B. T. 
Road, Belghoria, Calcutta-56 and their work- 
men represented by Himani Workers’ Union, 
Panja-Villa, P.O. Agarpara, 24-Parganas. 
(Case No. 374/67.) 


BEFORE THE FIFTH INDUSTRIAL 
TRIBUNAL, WEST BENGAL 


Present: 


Shri শা, K. MUTSUDDI, Judge, 
Fifth Industrial Tribunal. 


Present for the Company: Shri .کا‎ K. Moitra, 
Vice-President. Assam, West Bengal, Orissa 
and Bihar Employers Association. 


Present for the Union: Shri S: N. Banerji, 
Advocate. 


By Government of West Bengal, Labour Depart- 
ment, order No. 2520-1.R./IR/111.-181/67, dated the 
1411) June 1967, the present industrial dispute 
betwéen Messrs. Himani Private Ltd. and their 
worknren was referred ما‎ the Fifth Industrial 
Tribunal under section 10 of the Industrial Dis- 
putes Act, for adjudication upon’ 1116 issue 
mentioned below: 


Issue 
Bonus for 1965-66. 


On receipt of notice from the Tribunal, both 
the parties made their appearances and filed their 
respective written statements. 


Admittedly, the Company paid 4 per cent. bonus 
to the workers. It is the case of the workmen 
that they are entitled (0 12) per cent. bonus for 
the year 1965-66. 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, JANUARY 16, 1969 77 


The case of the Company is that it sustained 
loss during the relevant year and, as such, the 
workmen are not entitled to get more than 4 per 


‘cent. bonus. 


The Company has filed the balance-sheet and 
the calculation of available surplus for bonus for 
the year 1965-66. Ext. A is the balance-sheet, 
and Ext. B is the chart showing calculation of 
allocable surplus. The chart has been prepared 
according to the Payment of Bonus Act of 1965. 
It shows Debit Balance of Rs. 9,274. So it appears 
that there was no available surplus for bonus in 
respect of the year 1965-66. The correctness of 
the balance-sheet has not been challenged by the 
learned Advocate for the Union. It is, however. 
submitted by him that as the Company 
did not produce all the registers it main- 
tained in the office, it is to be taken that 
the entries in the  balance-sheet 26 not 
correct. I am unable to accept this conten- 
tion of the Union. Section 23 of the Payment of 
Bonus Act says that it should be presumed that 
the particulars and statements contained in the 
balance-sheet and profit and loss account are 
accurate unless proved otherwise by cogent evi- 
dence. In this case the Union has not called for 
the register3 maintained by the Company. Had 
the Union called for those documents, and had the 
Company refused to produce them, then and then 
only it could be inferred that the balance-sheet 
and the profit and loss account have not been 
correctly prepared. As no such steps have been 
taken by the Union, it must be presumed that the 
balance-sheet and the profit and loss account sub- 
mitted by the Company have been correctly 
prepared. Admittedly, bonus was paid to the 
workmen by the Company on the previous year al 
12} per cent. There is no item mentioned in the 
profit and loss account or in the balance-sheet that 
any rebate had been received by the Company 
from the Income Tax Department on account of 
payment of bonus to the workmen for the previ- 
ous year. So it is submitted by the learned Advo- 
cate for the Union that from this it should be 
taken that the balance-sheet and the profit and 
loss account submitted by the Company have not 
been correctly prepared. But there is no positive 
evidence that actually any rebate had been gran- 
ted to the Company by the Income Tax 
Department on account of payment bonus 
to the workmen during 1964-65, It may 
be that the Income Tax Department have 
not yet granted rebate to the Company. 
There is no evidence on the side ০1 the 
Union that any such rebate had been granted 
to the Company by the Income Tax Department. 
The balance-sheet does not show that any such 
rebate has been granted by the Income Tax 
Department. It should be presumed that the 
entries in the balance-sheet are correct. I, there- 
fore. find no reason as to why the balance-shect 
and the calculation of available surplus, as sub- 
mitted by the Company, should not be relied upon. 
I find that during the relevant year the Company 
had no available surplus. Under section 10 of the 
Payment of Bonus Act the Company has paid to 
the workmen bonus at the rate of 4 percent. The 
Company has done according to law. I find that

CALCUTTA IMPROVEMENT TRUST 


THE BOARD OF TRUSTEES FOR THE 
IMPROVEMENT OF CALCUTTA 


Notice under section 43 of the Calcutta Improvement 
Act, 1911 (Bengal Act V of 1911) 


Calcutta, the 3lst December 1968. 


Scheme No. XV-M (Supplementary) 


It is hereby notified under section 43 of the Calcutta 
Improvement Act, 1911, that a Rehousing Scheme for 
the construction of flats and shops for providing alter- 
Native accommodation mainly to the bustee-dwellers 
and shop-keepers to be displaced due to execution of 
Scheme No. XV-M (Widening of Manicktala Main 
Road between Scheme No. I-M and western flank of 
Railway Bridge) on a block of land in Scheme No. 
VI-M (Narkeldanga Main Road to Manicktala Main 
Road) and Scheme No. VII-M (Manicktala Main 
Road to Ultadanga Main Road), to be hereinafter 
known as Scheme No. XV-M (Supplementary), has 
been framed by the Board of Trustees for the Im- 
provement of Calcutta in constituency No. 32 of the 
Calcutta Corporation. 


2. The area comprised within and রা for the 
execution of the scheme (shown in yellow verge in 
the plan) measures 1.71 acres, more or less, and is 
more particularly described below:— 


Boundaries of the land 


On the North: Calcutta Improvement Trust

GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL 


HOME DEPARTMENT 
Transport 


NOTIFICATION 


No. 7661-WT.—24th July 1968.—In exercise of the power conferred by sub- 
section (1) of section 71 of the Calcutta Hackney-Carriage Act, 1919 (Bengal 
Act I of 1919), the Governor is pleased hereby to make the following by-laws 
for the Durgapur Notified Area (hereinafter referred to as the said Notified 
Area) in the district of Burdwan, namely:— 


BY-LAWS 


1. Definitions.—In these by-laws, unless there is anything repugnant in the 
subject or context,— 
(a) “The Act” means the Calcutta Hackney-Carriage Act, 1919 (Bengal 
Act I of 1919); 
(b) “Member” means a Member of the Durgapur Notified Area Authority; 


(c) “Rickshaw” means a cycle-rickshaw as defined in clause (8) of section 4 
of the Act. 


2. Appointment and duties of the Registering Officer.—Every Rickshaw 
in the Durgapur Notified Area (hereinafter referred to as the said Notified Area) 
shall be annually registered on such date as the members may direct, by a 
Registering Officer specially appointed for the purpose by the State Government 
by a Notification in the Official Gazette. The Registering Officer shall keep the 
registers in accordance with the provisions of the Act and shall enter therein 
the particulars specified in these by-laws. 


3. Qualifications and conditions for issue of bearer’s License.—Every 
person applying for a rickshaw bearer’s licence shall be required to satisfy the 
Registering Officer— 

(a) that he knows how to drive and control a rickshaw; 
(b) that he is well-acquainted with the principal streets, offices and places 
in and around the said Notified Area. 


244b 


2440 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, EXTRA ORDINERY, JANUARY 16, 1969 


(c) that he has a thorough knowledge of the tables of fares and distances 
prepared by the Commissioners in this behalf; 


(d) that he knows the rules of the road and the conventional signals used 
by the bearers and drivers of vehicles and by the Traffic police; 


(e) that he is between 18 and 45 years of age on the date of the 
application for issue of the Rickshaw bearer's license; and 


(f) that he is both physically and in all other respects a fit person for such 
employment. 


4. Contents of Jicense.—There shall be affixed to each license issued to the 
bearer of a rickshaw— 


(a) the thumb mark or the signature of the bearer; 
(b) a half-post card size photograph of the bearer to be supplied by him; 
and 


(c) a printed table of fares and distances prepared by the Commissioners, 
for which no charge shall have to be paid by the bearer. 


5. Production of license, etc.—Every bearer of a rickshaw shall carry with 
him his license and shall produce it whenever called upon to do so by any 
policeman on duty, any member or any other person authorised by the members 
in this behalf. 


6. Condition of rickshaws.—({1) The body of the rickshaw shall be kept 
sound and clean and all the boards shall be strong and properly secured. 


(2) The wheels shall be fitted with pneumatic tyres, and shall be strong and 
sound so as to run smoothly, without rattling or shaking and shall be protected 
by properly fitted splash boards. | 


(3) The springs and axles shall be of good metal, strong and properly 
rivetted and free from rust. 


(4) The iron support at the back which shall be of good metal, strong and 
free from rust shall be properly curved and securely fixed on each side. 


(5) The hood, apron and cushions shall be made of, and covered with, good 
cloth, canvas or other material approved of by the members at a meeting. 


(6) The shafts shall be of strong wood, securely fixed, furnished at the 
fore-end with a ring-shaped metal support and connected by a collision guard. 


ae The hood and apron shall be so fitted as to make the vehicle water- 
tight. 


(8) Every rickshaw shall have two good lamps—one facing the front and 
the other the rear. 


(9) The lamp facing the rear shall have a red glass-cover and shall be so 
placed that the light through the cover be visible from a point ten metres in the 
rear of the centre of the vehicle. 


(10) Each arm of the rickshaw shall be so constructed as to serve as a 
support to the passenger. 


(11) Every rickshaw shall have a bell or a horn, as may be approved of by 
the Commissioners, affixed to the handle bars or cross bars on the cycle in such 
a way that it can be operated by fingers and give continuous ringing as and when 
necessary. 


7. Dimensions and pattern of rickshaws.—Every rickshaw shall conform 
to the following dimensions and be of such pattern as may be specified by the 


Commissioners at a meeting:—

9. Rates and fares.—Fares shall be paid according to distance or time, at 
the option of the hirer, to be expressed at the commencement of hiring and if 
not so expressed, according to time.

10. Speed and halting charges of rickshaws.—When a rickshaw is hired, 
the bearer shall ordinarily drive the same at a speed of not less than thirteen 
kilometres per hour. If a rickshaw after being hired is made to halt, halting 
টা? shall be paid according to the scale laid down in the fare table in 

y-law 9. 


ll. Passengers are to pay other charges.—Passengers are to pay the ferry 
and other similar charges over and above the rates payable to the bearers of 
rickshaw. 


12. Prohibition of smoking, etc.—While driving, the bearer of a rickshaw 
shall not smoke or muffle up his face in such a manner as to endanger the 
proper driving of his vehicle. 


13. Maximum load to be carried in rickshaw.—The total weight of the 
passengers and the luggage, if any, carried in a rickshaw shall not exceed 
150 kilograms. 


14. Advertisement on rickshaws.—No advertisement shall be displayed on 
the body of a rickshaw without the previous permission of the Commissioners 
and when such permission is obtained, it shall be displayed in such a manner 
as not to cover either wholly or partly the number plate and the fare table 
affixed to the rickshaw. 


15. Rickshaws to wait at stand.—Every rickshaw while at rest, shall be 
parked at a stand fixed by the Commissioners for such purpose. 


16. Power of entry.—It shall be lawful for a Commissioner or any other 
person authorised in this behalf by the Chairman or the Commissioners, at 
any time between sun-rise and sun-set, to enter any premises in which any 
licensed rickshaw or any other thing used therewith are kept, in order to carry 
out any of the provisions of the Act or of these by-laws, and the owner or 
occupier of the premises or his agent, as the case may be, shall afford everv 
reasonable facility to such Commissioner or person for such inspection.

SUPPLEMENT—Official Papers 


BY-LAWS OF SAMCO ROPEWAY AT SHEPKHOLA 


Reang T.P.O., District Darjeeling 


1. General—The General By-Laws of the Samthar Co-operative 
Multipurpose Society Ltd., insofar as they concern the running of The Samco 
Ropeway, management, keeping the accounts, distributing the profits if any, 
etc., that apply to the Samco Ropeway in addition to the By-laws hereinafter 
expressed. 


2. Management.—The General Manager of Samco Project shall be respon- 
sible for running the Ropeway and all enquiries communications, complaints, 
etc., should be addressed to him by designation as the latter procedure may 
cause delay in cases of absence and not by name. 


3. Conduct of Ropeway Employees.—({a) Ropeway employees must be 
courteous and obliging to the members of the public and render them every 
assistance, subject to observance of rules. 


(b) Gratuities or fees or perquisites should not in any circumstances be 
asked for and obtained by the Ropeway employees. 


4. Time.—(a) Hours of business: Stations will be open for the booking 
and for delivery of parcels and goods between 7 and 12 hours and 13.30 and 
17 hours daily except on Sundays and national holidays. 


(b) Despatch by any particular time not guaranteed.—The Ropeway 
Company do not guarantee the despatch of parcels and goods by any particular 
time, nor will they be responsible for the arrival of parcels or goods by 
any particular time. 

5. Stations.—There shall only be (2) stations on the Ropeway namely: 

27th mile 


Shepkhola,

6. Traffic—(a) Passengers shall not be carried. 


(b) Large animals shall not be carried. Small animals may 8نا‎ carried 
provided they are properly confined in baskets and crates which will be 
weighed and charged for accordingly. 


(০) Luggage, parcels and goods are carried subject to the restrictions 
hereinafter as above. 


7. Booking.—Each consignment when tendered for despatch will be 
entered in a challan or forwarding note showing description, weight and fees 
to be charged and also marks of identification of the consignment. A copy 
of the same will be issued to the sender. 


8. Marking.—Every packing must be clearly marked by the sender with 
name or private marks for identification purposes and the same should also 
be entered in the challan. 


9. Dimensions and weight.—(a) The dimensions of any package should not 
be greater than the following:— 


Length 12 feet. 
Width 2 feet. 
Height 2 feet. 


(b) The weight of amy package should not be more than 200 kg. 


10. Rates.—Rates for goods, parcels, etc., will be charged as follows:— 


(a) Maximum: 
For 40 kg. loads Rs. 1.25. 
For 100 kg. loads Rs. 3.10. 
For 1 bag charcoal Re. 1.00. 
For 1 cubic foot of wood, planks Rs. 1.25. 
For 1,000 oranges Rs. 2.50. 


(0) Minimum: The above rates less 10 per cent. These rates of charges 
are subject to revision of which previous notice shall be displayed 
at the stations. 


(c) The above rates are inclusive of loading and unloading at the stations 
and loading into trucks at 27th mile. 


11. Risk.—All goods will be carried at the risk of the owners and the 
Ropeway concerned shall be kept harmless and free from all responsibility 
for any loss, destruction or deterioration of, or damage to, all or any of the 
consignments from any cause whatever except upon proof that the said loss, 
destruction, deterioration or damage arose from misconduct or gross negligence 
of the Ropeway administration or its servants. 


12. Notice of arrival—The Company does not undertake to serve notice 
to the consignee of arrival of parcels or goods. 


13, Wharfage.—All luggages, goods, etc., must be removed from the godown 
within a reasonable time which shall depend on the nature of the goods and 
its bulk. If ever a consignee unduly delays in taking delivery of his goods 
a wharfage charge of 10 paise per 40 kg. or part thereof per day or part thereof 
will be calculated after notice has been given in writing to the consignee. 


14. Partial delivery of consignments.—A consignee must take delivery 
of luggage, parcels or goods, forming part of a consignment whenever they 
are available for delivery, notwithstanding the fact that the reminder of the 
consignment is short or damaged or has not arrived at destination or is other- 
wise not available for delivery. If a consignee does not take delivery of such 
luggage, parcels or goods, forming part of a consignment as are available for 
delivery, they will be subject to the usual wharfage charges, if not removed 
within the free time allowed.

15. Disfigured receipts—Ropeway receipts should on no account be 
altered disfigured or mutilated, and the same will not be accepted if so 
altered, disfigured or mutilated. 


16. Delivery when Ropeway receipt is lost.—When a Ropeway receipt has 
been lost, mislaid, or is for other reason not forthcoming, the company reserv- 
ed the right to demand an indemnity bond before giving delivery of the. 
articles concerned. 


17 Time limit of claims for refund or compensation.—No person shall be 
entitled to a_ refund of an overcharge in respect of goods carried by our 
Ropeway or to compensation for the loss, destruction or deterioration of goods 
delivered to be so carried, unless his claim to the refund or compensation has 
been preferred in writing by him or on his behalf to the Ropeway within six 
months from the date of the delivery of the goods for carriage by the Ropeway 
(Chapter V, seetion 39 of the Bengal Aerial Ropeway Act, 1923). 


Carriage of: 


18. Offensive goods.—The following shall be deemed to be offensive goods, 
namely:— 


(1) Blood dried, (2) Bones, (3) Carcasses of dead animals, (4) Corpses, (5) 
Decayed animal or vegetable matter, (6) Manures of any kind 
creel chemical manures, (7) Municipal or Street-sweepings or 
refuse. 


Consignment of offensive goods shall only be accepted for conveyance, 
subject to the following conditions, namely:— 


(1) The loading, unloading and transhipment of the offensive goods shall 
be done by the consignor and consignee or other servants; and 


(2) Freight shall be prepaid by the consignor. 


19. Dangerous goods.—No explosives as defined in the Indian Explosives 
Act or the dangerous, corrosive and poisonous chemicals shall be accepted for 
conveyance by the Ropeway. 


20. Booking.—In cases of heavy bookings special arrangements may be made 
in advance with the Superintendent concerned. 


21. Penalties and fines——Any person who contravenes the provisions of 
any of the by-laws shall be liable to a fine which may extend to any sum not 
exceeding fifty rupees. In the case of a breach of a by-laws regulating the 
conduct of Ropeway employees the servant responsible for the same shall 
forfeit a sum not exceeding one month’s pay which sum will be deducted from 
his pay.

fifteenth day of January one thousand nine hundred

INDIA, a Corporation established under the Reserve

AGREEMENT 


MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT made this 
Sixteenth day of January One thousand nine 
hundred and sixty-nine between Messrs. WESTERN 
BENGAL COAL-FIELDS LIMITED, a Company 
registered under the Indian Companies Act, 1913 
and having its Registered Office at 15, India 
Exchange Place, Calcutta-1 (hereinafter called ‘The 
Company”) of the ONE PART, and the GOVERNOR 
of the State of West Bengal (hereinafter called “The 
Governor”) of the OTHER PART. 


WHEREAS for the purpose of construction of a 
Higher Secondary School and other allied buildings, 
the Company has applied to the Government of West 
Bengal for the acquisition under the provisions of 
the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred 
to as the said “Act’’), of the piece or parcel of land 
containing 2.87 acres or thereabout situate in the 
mauza of Mahira, police-station Ondal in the district 
of Burdwan and more particularly described in the 
Schedule hereto and delineated in the “plan here- 
unto annexed; 


AND WHEREAS the said Government of West 
Bengal (hereinafter referred to as the “Government”) 
upon the advice of the Land Acquisition Committee 
constituted under rule 3 of the Land Acquisition 
(Companies) Rules (hereinafter referred to as the 
said “Rules’) and after consideration of the 
Collector’s report under rule 4 of the said Rules and 
being satisfied on the report of the Collector under 
section 40 of the said Act that such acquisition is 
needed for the construction of the building or work 
of the Company which is engaged in an industry or 
work which is for a public purpose; has given its 
consent to acquire on behalf of the Company the 
piece or parcel of land as hereunder described in the 
Schedule;

Whereas it appears to the Governor that land is 
likely to be needed for a public purpose, namely, for 
the construction for development of capacity for 
movement of Oil Traffic for Assam Railway Link 
(Mile 28-29) in the villages of Dangi, Manora and: 
Lahil, jurisdiction list Nos. 181, 165 and 166 
respectively, thana Goalpukhar, pargana Surjapur, 
zilla West Dinajpur, it is hereby notified that pieces 
of land as described in the Schedules “A” and “B” 
below and measuring altogether, more or less, 4.8643 
hectares (12.02 acres), are likely to be needed for the 
aforesaid public purpose at the public expense within, 
the aforesaid villages of Dangi, Manora and Lahil. 


This notification is made, under the provisions of 
section 4 of Act 1 of 1894, to all whom it may concern, 


A plan of the land may be inspected in the office 
of the Collector West Dinajpur, Balurghat. 


In exercise of the powers conferred by the afore- 
said section the Governor is pleased to authorise the, 
officers for the time being engaged in the under- 
taking, with their servants and workmen, to enter 
upon and survey the land and do all other acts 
required or permitted by that section. 

Whereas the Governor is satisfied that the lands 
described in the schedules below are urgently needed 
for the aforesaid public purpose, the Governor, in 
exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (4) 
of section 17 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1 of 1894, 
is pleased to direct that the provisions of section SA 
of the Act shall not apnly to the said lands which are 
entirely waste and arable and to which, in the opinion 
of Governor, the provisions of sub-section (1) of 
section 17 of the said Act are applicable.

tution of India;

likely to be needed for a public purpose, namely, for 
development of capacity for movement of Oil Traffic 
for Assam Rail Link (mile 50-51), in the villages of 
‘Ikarchala, jurisdiction list No. 17/43 (old), Majhok,

zilla West Dinajpur, it is hereby notified that pieces 
of land as described in the Schedules “A” and “B” 
below and measuring altogether, more or 1655, 
1.7765 hectares (4.39 acres), is likey to be needed for

within the aforesaid villages of Ikrachala, Majhok,

۱ Whereas the Governor is satisfied that the lands

COVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL

۱ Audit 
NOTIFICATION 
No. 297-F/4L-19/68.—18th January 1969.—The Governor 15 pleased to 
make the following rules, namely :— 
Preliminary 
5ْ (1) These rules may be called the West Bengal State Lottery Rules, 


(2) They shall apply to the whole of the State of West Bengal and shall 
come into force at once. 


2. The West Bengal State Lottery (hereinafter referred to as the State 
Lottery) shall be administered by the Director of State Lotteries, West Bengal, 
Calcutta (hereinafter referred to as “the Director’), under the control of the 
Government of West Bengal (hereinafter referred to as “the Government”). 


Lottery Tickets and Prizes 


3. (1) Tickets for every draw of the State Lotteries shall be issued in the 
denomination of rupees two only, provided that the Government shall have 
the power to change the price of all the tickets for any draw or draws aiter 
due publicity before the commencement of the sale of tickets for such draw. 


(2) Tickets shall be issued in distinct and separate series; each such serics 
shall be distinguished by a distinct alphabetical notation. 


(3) Each such series shall consist of 999999 tickets and shall be numbered 
consecutively from 000001 to 999999. 


4, (1) The number and amount of prizes for each draw shall be 
determined and announced by the Government from time time before the 
commencement of the sale of tickets for such draw. 


(2) All prizes are guaranteed by the Government. 


(3) No ticket shall'be eligible for more than one prize in a draw. In the 
event of more than one prize being drawn against a particular ticket, the ticket 
holder shall be entitled only to the prize drawn first in chronological order 
against his ticket and there shall be a fresh draw for the lower prize. 


(4) Tickets remaining unsold with the office of the Director shall not be 
eligible for any prize in a draw. If an unsold ticket number is drawn, the 
process of the draw shall be repeated till a sold number is drawn.

Sale of Lottery Tickets and Appointment of Agents 


5. The State Lottery tickets will normally be made available to the public 
through authorised agents and such other channels as may be determined 
from time to time by the Government. The Government also reserve the 
right to sell tickets direct to the public. 


6. Notices inviting applications for appointment as agents shall be widely 
published. Application forms will be available at the office of the Director 
in Calcutta and at such other places as may be notified by the Director from 
time to time. 


7. (1) The appointment of agents shall be made by the Director and such 
other authorities as may be nominated by the Government in this behalf from 
time to time and it shall be open to the Director or other appointing authority 
to terminate the appointment of any agent without assigning any reason. In 
appointing agents due consideration shall be given to the financial status of 
the applicant, his ability to promote sale of tickets and any other factor which 
the Director or other appointing authority may consider relevent in that 
behalf. 

The decision of the Director or other appointing in the matter of the 
appointment of an agent and the termination of his appointment shall be final 
and binding and nv appeal shall be entertained against the decision. 


(2) The Director shall have the right to restrict the number of agents for 
a particular area. 


(3) The appointment of an agent shall be valid for a period of two months 
from the date of appointment or for a particular draw, whichever is shorter, 
unless the period is extended by the Director or other appointing authority. 
The agents shall, on production of the order of appointment, be entitled to 
purchase tickets from the office of the Director and Treasuries and Sub- 
Treasuries in the State mentioned in the order of appointment. 


(4) Tickets shall be sold to the agents only in books containing fifty tickets 
rat except for the iast book of each series which will contain only forty-nine 
tickets. ٠ 
‘ 0 Tickets once sold to the agents shall, under no circumstances, be taken 

ack: 

Provided that if any defective tickets are sold to any agent through over- 
sight, such tickets shall be received back by the Director up to the fifth da 
aiter the sale and the price thereof shall be refunded to the agent concerned. 


_ (6) The agents shall purchase tickets on payment of the full value of the 
tickets less commission allowable on the face value of the tickets. 


8. (1) The agent shall be eligible for a commission of 15 per cent. on the 
face value of the tickets purchased by them. 


(2) A special cominission shall be allowed in the following cases, namely:— 


(i) 2 per cent, extra in cases where purchases made by an agent for a draw 
excced five thousand tickets. 


(ii) 5 per cent., i.e., 20 per cent. in all extra in cases where purchases made 
by an agent for a draw exceed fifty thousand tickets. 


If purchases of tickets mentioned above are made in _ instalments, the 
special commission shall be paid only after the close of the draw. 


_ 9. Tickets shall be issued to the agents up to seven clear days before the date 
fixed for the draw. Agents may, however, sell tickets till the date immediately 
preceding the date of the draw. All tickets sold to ayents shall be deemed to 
be ‘sold tickets’ for the purposes of the draw and the award of prizes. 


Draw of the Lottery 


10. The date of the draw shall generally be indicated on the tickets 
themselves. 


The Director shall have the right to postpone the date of the draw. Due 
publicity shall, however, be given to such postponement and also to the revise 
date of the draw. 


The time when and the place where the draw will be held shall a!so be given 
wide publicity. |

11. The draw shall be held in public and under the supervision of a Com- 
mittee of Judges specially appointed by the Government for the purpose. The 
Committee of Judges shall consist of not less than five Judges including a High 
Court Judge, if available. At any time, during the draw two Judges shall form 
the quorum. 


12. A list duly authenticated by the Director indicating the notations of the 
series of tickets sold and a list of number issued in the series shall be furnished 
to the Committee of Judges. A list of tickets remaining unsold with the office 
of the Director shall also be drawn up by the Director and shall also be 
furnished to the Committee of Judges, duly authenticated by him, before the 
draw commences. 


13. As soon as a particular number is drawn in the manner indicated in rule 
19, the prize winning-number shall be entered in the Register of the Prize- 
winning Numbers kept in the personal custody of the Director. The Judges 
present shall sign the Register as soon as the draw is completed. This procedure 
shall be repeated till all prizes for the draw are drawn. 


14. After the draw is over, the records shall be kept in the custody of the 
office of the Director for such period as the Government may determine. 


15. Due publicity shall be given to the list of prize-winning tickets but the 
list as published in the “Calcytta Gazette” shall alone constitute the official 
announcement of the results of each draw. 


Procedure for the Draw 


16. The procedure for the draw shall be as follows: 


There shall be seven drums located in a conspicuous place at one end of the 
hall where the draw is conducted. The drums shall bear the following 
identification labels, namely:— 


I 11 111 IV V VI VII 
Alphas Lekhs Tenthou- Thourands. Hundreds. Tens. Units. 
betical sands. 
series. 


17. The first drum shall contain twice as many discs as there may be 
alphabetical notations, two discs for each notation, used in the different series 
of tickets issued for sale in a draw. Each one of the other six drums shall 
contain thirty discs each of the digits from 0 to 9 being inscribed on three discs. 
To prevent confusion the digits 6 and 9 shall be inscribed in words, namely, 
‘SIX’ and ‘NINE’. Each drum _ shall be such as may be mechanically or 
electrically rotated and the rotation shall be stopped as and when directed by the 
Committee of Judges. The drums shall be rotated by persons duly upproved 
by the Committee of Judges. 


A Notice Board shall be displayed in a prominent place in the drawing hall 
where the alphabetical notations and the digits drawn from each drum shall be 
recorded as soon as the same are drawn from each drum. 


18. (1) Prizes will be drawn in the descending order of the value of the 
prizes, the first prizes, the first prize being drawn first and the last one being 
drawn last. 


(2) The draw shall commence from the first drum and shall be followed in 
the ascending order of the number given to each of the other drums.‘ As soon 
as an alphabetical notation or a digit is drawn, it shall be announced loudly by 
the person drawing it, and after verification by the Committee of Judges, it shall 
be displayed on the Notice Board. 


Payment of Prizes 


19. (1) The winners of prizes shall claim the prize amounts from the 
Director. The first and the second prizes may be handed over at ceremonial 
{functions which may be organised for this purpose by the Director as soon after 
the conclusion of the draw as may be possible. 


(2) Prizes shall be awarded direct to the winners only on surrendering the 
prize-winning tickets at the office of the Director. The persons who will 
actually produce the prizc-winning tickets shall be deemed to be the purchasers 
of the tickets and, therefore, the prize winners. Prizes may be paid in person 
or sent by post through the Reserve Bank of India drafts on receipt of the prize- 
winning ticket as well as a signed receipt in the prescribed form.

20. Prize amounts must be claimed within thirty days after the date of the 
publication of the results of the draw in the “Calcutta Gazette”. Prize amounts 
not claimed within the said thirty days shall lapse and be automatically 
forfeited to the Government. 


21. The Government shall not recognise the re-sale in full or in part of a 
ticket or any transfer thereof. 


Supplemental Matters 


22. The Government reserve the right to alter or modify these rules from 
time to time. Such changes shall, however, be duly notified in the “Calcutta 
Gazette”. The terms regarding the price of the tickets, the number and value 
of the prizes and the procedure for drawal of prize-winning tickets shall not, 
however, be altered in respect of any draw after the commencement of the sale 
of tickets for that draw. 


23. If any question arises as to the interpretation of any of these rules or 
in regard to any matter not expressly provided for in these rules, the matter 
shall be ا‎ to the Government and the decision of the Government thereon 
shall be final. 


By order of the Governor, 


۲ C. BANERJI, 
Jt. Secy. to the Govt. of West Bengal.

GOVERNOR’S SECRETARIAT, WEST BENGAL 


NOTIFICATION 


No, 438-S.—llth January 1969.—The Governor is 
pleased to award the “Dr. Harendra Coomar 
Mookerjee Silver Medal’’ for the year 1967 to the 
undermentioned persons for outstanding acts of 
courage and self-sacrifice:— 


Name and address of the person 


]. Shr Bhagirath Prasad Roy, Student, Labpur 
Jadab Lal High School, Birbhum. 


Statement of the act performed for which the 
decoration has been awarded 


On 26th August 1967, at about 5 pm., two 
Santhal girls were engaged in transplantation of 
paddy in a plot of land by the side of a river. The 
attention of the girls having been drawn to a few 
bundles of paddy seedlings floating down the river, 
they felt tempted to have them and went into the 
river, But, unfortunately, as soon as they reached 
the river bed they were caught in the forceful 
current of the flood water in the river and were 
being swept away. At that time Shri  Bhagirath 
Prasad Roy, a student of Labpur Jadav Lal High 
School, was seated on the nearby ralway bridge 
with his friends and classmates. When __ the 
unfortunate incident came to his notice, he rushed 
to the river bank, cast off his cloths, plunged into 
the water and swam to a distance of 25/30 cubits, 
Coming close to one of the girls he first caught her 
by the lock of hair, but she was making a frantic 
attempt to clasp him, So, he let her go for a 
while and immediately with great alacrity and pluck 
he caught her again both by the hair and one of her 
hands and successfully dragged her ashore with all 
possible force. Meanwhile, he had perceived ۶٤۴ 
touch of some other human body moving down 
slowly under the flood water. So he hurried back 
to the river bed, dived deep into the water, made 
a frantic search to trace the body out and ultimately 
succeeded in this venture too. It was a 58115601695 
body of the other Santhal girl that required tremend- 
ous force, being very heavy, to be taken ashore, 
After first-aid was administered, both the girls 
gradually regained their senses and became normal 
and they were made over to their relatives who 
showered profuse blessings on Bhagirath. 


In rescuing successively two drowning girls from 
a river in high spate at great personal risk and 
danger, Shri Bhagirath Prasad Roy _ displayed 
exemplary courage and spirit of self-sacrifice. 


Name and address of the person 


2. Shri Narayan Chakraborty, Sub-Inspector, 
South Port Police Station, Port Division, 
Calcutta Police. 


Statement of the act performed for which the 
decoration has been awarded 


On 13th May 1967 at about 11 a.m. Sub-Inspector, 
Narayan Chakraborty while about to get ashore after 
finishing his bath in the Ganges at Watgunge, 
Calcutta, heard’a hue and cry raised by the bathers 
and all those standing on the shore that someone 
was getting drowned. Shri Chakraborty looked 
back and could see only the wrists of a drowning 
man, who was making frantic efforts to catch hold 
of something, but was being carried towards the 
midstream due to a whirl. Of all persons present 
there, it was Shri Chakraborty, who pondered for 
a moment, took his decision, girded up his loins 
and plunged headlong into the river in full spate 
in complete disregard of his personal safety and 
quickly reached the drowning man. He _ caught 
hold of his wrist, dragged him out of the whirl and 
brought him to the shore like an expert life saver. 


In saving the life of a drowning man from a river 
in full spate at great personal risk and under most 
hazardous circumstances, Sub-Inspector Chakraborty 
displayed outstanding courage, deep sense of civic 
duty and spirit of self-sacrifice. 


Name and address of the person 


3. Shri Aswini Kumar Roy, Assistant Sub- 
Inspector, Beliaghata Police Station, 
Calcutta. 


Statement of the act performed for which the 
decoration has been awarded 


On 14th January 1967 at about 1-55 a.m., while 
on night rounds, Assistant Sub-Inspector Aswini 
Kumar Roy of Beliaghata Police Station heard a 
groaning sound from the direction of the canal, 
Soon he discovered a man Struggling in the water 
of the canal to save himself from being drowned. 
It was apparent that the man was utterly exhausted 
and would give up the struggle before long. The 
Assistant Sub-Inspector, who was.in full uniform, 
lost no time in jumping into the canal, in complete 
disregard of his personal safety, and after a good 
deal of struggle in the water succeeded in rescuing 
the man from the clutches of almost certain death. 
First-aid was administered to the man, who was 
pulled out in a Senseless condition and was in a 
State of profound shock, After quite 50170 time, 
the man who was fairly old gave out his name as 
Bepin Das. The General Diary of Beliaghata Police 
Station revealed that a man of the same name had 
been reported as missing. Later, the old man, aged 
79 years who was a short sighted and insane person 
and had slipped out of his house unnoticed by his 
relations, was restored to his family. 


In rescuing a drowning man under extremely 
hazardous circumstances disregarding fll personal 
risks and dangers, Assistant Sub-Inspector Aswini 
Kumar Roy displayed exemplary courage and 
resolve, deep sense of civic duty, spirit of  self- 
sacrifice and mental alacrity. 


By order of the Governor, 
D. W. TELANG, 


Secretary to the Governor, 
West Bengal,

DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH 
Medical 
NOTIFICATION 


No. Medl/107/1H-176/68.—7th January 1969.—In_ exercise of the 
power conferred by section 8 of the R. G. Kar Medical College and Hospital 
Act, 1958 (West Bengal Act No. VIII of 1958), the Governor is pleased 
hereby to make the following rules, namely ے‎ 

THE R. 6. KAR MEDICAL COLLECE AND HOSPITAL ADVISORY 
COMMITTEE RULES, 1998. 


1. These rules may be called the R. (03. Kar Medical College and Hospi- 


tal Advisory Committee Rules, 1968. 


2. In these rules, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or 


context,— 


(1) et ند‎ means the R. G. Kar Medical College and Hospital Act, 


(2) ‘Chairman’? means the Chairman of the Advisory Committee and 
for the purposes of rules 6, 7 and 8 includes a member elected 
under rule 6 to preside over any meeting; 

(3) ““Government”? means the Government of West Bengal; 

(4) “‘meeting’’ means a meeting of the Advisory Committee; 

(6) ‘‘Member’’ means a member of the Advisory Committee; 

(6) ‘‘Principal-Superintendent’’ means the Principal-Superintendent of 


the institution ; 


) “‘Quarter’’ means a period of three calendar months: 
(8) ‘Secretary’? means the Secretary of the Advisory Committee. 
3. The Secretary shall, on the direction of the Chairman, convene 
meetings of the Advisory Committee as often as the business of the institu- 
tion may require, ,مہ‎ however, that at least one such meeting shall be held 


in every quarter. 


4. Save as otherwise hereinafter provided, at least one week’s notice of 
every meeting shall be given to the members and such notice shall include 


the agenda: 


Provided that in the case of an emergent meeting, twenty-four hours’ 


notice shall be sufficient. 


5. Six members shall form a quorum. 

6. The Chairman shall, if present, preside over every meeting. In the 
absence of the Chairman from any meeting, the members present shall elect 
one from amongst themselves to preside over that meeting. 

7. The proceedings of all meetings shall be recorded by the Secretary 
and shall be authenticated by the Chairman. 


_ 8. (1) Except where the members are unanimous, any matter under 
discussion at any meeting shall be decided by the votes of the majority of 


the members present and voting. 


(2) Every member shall have one vote. The Chairman shall not vole, 
but shall, in the case of an equality of votes, have a casting vote. 
(3) The votes shall be taken by show of hands or by division as che 


Chairman may think fit: 


174 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, JANUARY 23, 1969 


SS ےو‎ 
—z موہ ہے ھے‎ ee oe ee 


STS জল আও CEE RIES. aE 


Provided that votes shall be taken by division where votes have already 
been taken by show of hands and any member asks for o division. 


(4) The procedure for taking votes by division shall be such as may be 
determined by the Chairman. 


(5) The result of voting shall be announced by the Chairman at the 
meeting and such announcement shall be final and shall not be challenged. 


9. The functions of the Committee shall be advisory. The Committee 
will advise in matters relating to the improvement of working conditions 
of the R. G. Kar Medical College I[ospital. The Committee shall also con- 
sider those matters relating to the teaching and administration of the R. G. 
Kar Medical College on which the College Council may choose to consult 
the Advisory Committee, and give their views and suggestions. 


10. The Members of the Advisory Committee shall visit the R. G. Kar 
Medical College Hospital and different Departments of the College in groups 
of not less than three members. Each group in turn shall, according to a 
roster to be kept for the purpose, visit the Hospital and/or the different 
Departments of the College on a fixed day and at a fixed time in each month. 
If all the three members of the group are not present during one of these 
rounds the members who are present shall go round in company with the 
Principal-Superintendent or in his absence the Vice-Principal or the Deputy 
Superintendent, 


11. In addition to these visits the members may, if they so desire, pay 
unexpected visits to the Hospital and such Departments of the College as 
the Principal may invite them to do. Members while paving such surpise 
visits should on arrival at the institution contact the Principal-Superin- 
tendent immediately or in his absence the Vice-Principal or aks Deputy- 
Superintendent and enter the Wards or the Departments as the case may 
be, in company with the Principal-Superintendent or the Vice-Principal 
or the Deputy Superintendent, as the case may be. | 


The members of the Committee during such rounds may inspect the 
working conditions and arrangements of the Department or Departments 
concerned and offer such suggestions as they may think proper and have 
them entered in the Visitors’ Book provided for the purpose. 


12. The Principal-Superintendent shall note on the margin of the 
Visitors’ Book the action taken on each recommendation of the Committee 
with such other remarks or explanations as he may wish to offer. He shall 
forward a copy of the entries immediately to the Director of Health Servi- 
ces, West Isengal, for consideration. The Director of Health Services, West 
Bengal, may take such further action on the matter as may seem to him 
to be necessary and may bring to the notice of the Government any matter 
which he thinks sufticiently important, 


13. The Committee as a whole shall meet at least once a quarter, 
review the recommendations of the Visiting Groups and discuss the remedial 
measures adopted. 


14, The Secretary shall send copies of the proceedings of every meeting 
as well as copies of the resolutions passed at 9 quarterly meetings to the 
members for information. Copies of the proceedings as well as copies of the 
resolutions should also be sent to the Secretary to the Government of West 
Bengal, Department of Health aud also to the Director of Health Services 
West Bengal, who shall submit to the Government a report on the action 
taken or proposed to be taken on the points raised in the resolutions. 


15. The Committee shall consider such other matters as may be placed 
before it by the Secretary either in his own discretion or at the direction 
of the Director of Health Services, West Bengal, and shall offer their sug- 
gestions and recommendations thereon. 


16. No act or proceeding of the Advisory Committee shall be called in 
question or invalidated merely by reason of the existence of a vacancy or 
vacancies amongst its members, or of any member not having been duly

ORDER 


No. 31-Power/3L-19/68. — 7th January 1969. — 
Whereas Shri Indra Mohan Roy has entered into an 
agreement with the Calcutta Electric Supply 
Corporation Limited, Licensees of the Calcutta and 
District Consolidated Electric Licence, 1946 (herein- 
after referred to as the said licensees), for taking 
from the said licensees, the supply of energy at his 
premises at Serampore Colony, Serampore, in the 
district of Hooghly, situated outside the area of 
supply of the said licensees; 


And whereas the said premises are not situated 
within the area of supply of any other licensee;. : 


Now, therefore, in exercise of the power con- 
ferred by section 27 of the Indian Electricity Act, 
1910 (Act 9 of 1910), the Governor is pleased to 
authorise the said licensees to supply energy to the 
said Shri Indra Mohan Roy at his premises at 
Serampore Colony, Serampore, in the district of 
Hooghly, for domestic purposes and to lay down and 
place electric supply lines for that purpose subject. 
to the following conditions 800 restrictions, 
namely :— 


The authority hereby conferred shall— 
(a) remain in force until— 


(i) the area of supply of the said licensees is 
extended so as_ to include within its 
limits the said premises of Shri Indra. 
Mohan Roy at Serampore Colony, Seram- 
pore, district Hooghly, or 


(ii) a licence is granted to any other person 
whose area of supply includes the said 
premises within its boundaries and such 
person is in a position to supply energy 
to the said premises, or এ 


(iii) any transmission or distribution system for 
supplying energy outside the area of 
supply of the said licensees is established 
by or on behalf of the State Electricity 
Board, 

enabling energy to be supplied at the said 
premises without such authority; and 


(b) be subject to the restrictions referred to in 
the third proviso to section 27 hereinbefore 


mentioned. 
By order of the Governor, 
M. K. ROY, Dy. Secy.

No. 12906-V.—27th December 1968.—In exercise - 
of the power conferred by the proviso to Article 309 
of the Constitution of India, the Governor is pleased 
hereby to make the following rules regulating the 
recruitment to the post of Superintendent of 
Veterinary Services, Artificial Insemination, under 
the scheme for establishment of the Central Semen 
Collection Centre at Belgachia, in the West Bengal 
Veterinary Service, under the Directorate of Veteri- 
nary Services, Government of West Bengal. 
namely : — 


Rules 


The method of recruitment and the qualifications 
required for recruitment to the post of Superin- 
tendent of Veterinary Services, Artificial Insemina- 
tion, under the scheme for establishment of the 
Central Semen Collection Centre at Belgachia, in the 
West Bengal Veterinary Service, under the Direc- 
torate of Veterinary Services, Government of West 
Bengal, shall be as detailed below: 


1. Method of recruitment:— 


Selection by direct recruitment, departmental 
candidates having requisite qualifications being 
eligible to apply. 


2. Qualifications:— 
A. Essential: 


(i) Membership of the Royal College of 
Veterinary Surgeons, United Kingdom; or 
a degree or diploma in Veterinary Science 
of a recognised University or Institution; 


(11) at least three years’ experience of Vetert- 
nary work in rural areas; 


(iii) at least two years’ experience of clinical 
work in a Veterinary Hospital; 


(iv) specialised training in Artificial Insemina- 
tion and Semen Preservation in a recog- 
nised Institution; 


(v) knowledge of Bengali--spoken and written. 


Note.—The experience required under items (ii) 
and (iii) above may be waived for a 
candidate holding the Membership of the 
Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons or a 
Master’s degree in Veterinary Science. 


B. Desirable: 


(i) A post-graduate degree or:: diploma 11 
Animal Genetics of a _ recognised 
University or Institution; 


() experience in maintenance of breeding bulls 
and treatment of animals with reprodue- 
tive disorders; 


(iii) administrative experience. 


PART I] 


ia fs —_—_s = =o ee = - 
سم‎ 


C. Age: 


Candidates shall not ordinarily be below 25 
years or above 35 years of age on the 3151 
December of the year in which the adver- 
tisements are issued. The age limit may be 
relaxed in the cases of candidates possess- 
ing exceptionally high qualifications or in 
the cases of candidates holding substantive 
appointments under the Central or a State 
Government. 


By order of the Governor, 
S. S. MUKHERJEE, Asst. Secy.

General 


For the Company : 


By the Government of West Bengal, Labour Depart- 
ment, order No. 5139-I.R./IR/11L-457/67, dated the 
27th September 1967, an industrial dispute between. 
Messrs. Chharia Commercial Private Ltd., 23-A Netaji 
Subhas Road, Calcutta-1, and their workmen represent- 
ed by Cossipore Mazdoor Sava, 90 B. T. Road, 
Calcutta-2, was referred under section 10 of the Indus- 
trial Disputes Act, 1947, to this Tribunal for adjudica- 
tion in respect of the following issues : 


Issues 


1. Grades and Scales of pay. 
2. Dearness Allowance. 


3. Whether the lock-out of the factory is justified ? 
To what relief, if any, are the workmen 
entitled ? 


Usual notices were served on the Company as well as 
the Union after receipt of the order of reference. 
Both the Union, as well as the Company appeared. 
Mazdoor Sava filed its written statement on 14th 


80 THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, JANUARY 23, 1969 


[PART IC 


November 1967. The Company, on the other hand, 
filed their written statement on 22nd July 1968. Since 
this date, neither the Company nor the Mazdoor Sava, 
it appears, is taking any interest in the matter of pro- 
ceeding with the hearing of the instant order of refe- 
rence. After 22nd July 1968, this case was fixed on 
12th August 1968, for filing list of documents by the 
parties. None appeared on 12th August 1968 and no 
list of documents was filed by either party. Then 26th 
September 1968, was fixed for fixing a date of hearing 
and on that date, the case was fixed on 11 
December 1968, for hearing. Neither the Company nor 
Mazdoor Sava appeared on 11th December 1968, an 

I gave a chance to the parties and fixed today (28th 
December 1968) for hearing of this order of reference. 
Today also neither the Company nor anybody on behalf 
of the Mazdoor Sava, has appeared on call. Shri S. 
N. Banerji, Advocate for the Company, on 0811, has 
stated before me that he has got no instructions from 
his clients to proceed with the hearing of this order of 
reference. Thus, it is quite clear that neither party is 
at all interested in the matter of proceeding with the 
hearing of this order of reference, and that there is no 
dispute between the Company as well as the Mazdoor 
Sava over the issues sent for adjudication to this 
Tribunal. 


Accordingly, I pass a ‘no-dispute’ award in this 
case. 


This is my award.

BEFORE THE FIFTH INDUSTRIAL TRIBUNAL, 
WEST BENGAL 


Present : 


Shri T. K. MUTSUDDI, Judge, 
Fifth Industrial Tribunal. 


Present for the Company: Shri C. L. Ganguly, 


Advocate. 
Present for the Union: Shri N. R. Roy, Advocate. 


By the Government of West Bengal, Labour Depart- 
ment, order No. 4236-I.R./IR/10L-6/67, dated the 219 
August 1967, this industrial dispute between Messrs. 
The National Insulated Cable Co. of India Ltd., and their 
workmen represented by the NICCO Canteen Shramik 
Union was referred to this Tribunal under section 10 
of the Industrial Disputes Act for adjudication upon 
the issue mentioned below. 


Issue 


Is the management justified in employing contract 
labour in the canteen? Should the system of 
contract labour be abolished? What relief, if 
any, are the wokmen employed in the canteen 
entitled to? 


On receipt of the notice from the Tribunal both the 
parties made appearance and filed their respective 
written statement. 


The Company takes a preliminary objection as to 
the maintainability of the reference. It is submitted 
on behalf of the Company that the reference itself 
shows that there is no relationship of employer and 
employee between the parties and, as such, it should 
be held that the reference is not maintainable. 


The issue in this case is whether the management is 
justified in employing contract labour in the canteen 
and whether the system of contract labour should be 
abolished. So this issue goes to indicate that contract 
labour system is existing in the canteen. The Union’ 
has adduced evidence to prove that their js 16 system 
of contract labour in the canteen. So, at present the 
Union does not admit existence of the system of con- 
tract Jahour in the canteen. The real question in this 
case is whether there is a relationship of employer and 
employees between the Company and the workmen. 
The Company has adduced evidence to prove that the 
canteen is being run by a contractor, and that ~ the 
workers working in the canteen are direct employees 
of the.contractor. The Union, on the other hand, has 
led evidence 10 prove that the workmen are direct 
employees of the Company. P.W. 1 Kalipada Biswas 
and P.W. 2 Shankar Kumar Ghosh were workers work- 
ing in the canteen. They want to say that they were 
appointed py the Company. But their oral evidence 


PART IC] 


THE CALCUTTA GAZETTE, JANUARY 23, 1969 81 


- =~ oN oa ০ ০ OS ES AETED 
১১১১8 হা ০ 


has not been supported by any documentary evidence. 
O.P.W. 2 G. S. Mohanat and O.P.W. 3 P. D. Pathak 
are officers of the Company. Their evidence is that 
the workers working in the canteen are not workers 
under the Company, and that they are direct employees 
of the contractor. The Company has produced some 
papers to show that the canteen is being run by a con- 
tractor. But there is no convincing documentary 
evidence to indicate that the workers of the canteen 
are direct employees under the contractor. The onus 
is on the Union to prove by cogent evidence that the 
workers of the canteen are direct employees of the 
Company. In order to maintain the reference the 
Union has to show that an industrial dispute exists 
between the parties. Industrial dispute means any 
dispute or difference between the employer and their 
employees. But in this case the Union has hopelessly 
failed to prove that the workers of the canteen are 
employees of the Company. So it has not been proved 
that an industrial dispute exists between the parties. 
In the circumstances, it should be held that the refer- 
ence is not maintainable. The Union has led evidence 
to prove that the Company itself runs the canteen, and 
that there is no contractor for the running of 116 
canteen. If this contention of the Union is accepted, 
then also it should be held that the reference is not 
maintainable. It must be held that the issues in the 
reference have not been properly framed. The issue 
is whether the management is_ justified in employing 
contract labour, and whether the system of contract 
labour should be abolished. So, if there is no exist- 
ence of contract labour, the questions whether the 
management is justified in employing contract labour 
and whether this system should be abolished do not 
arise at-all. In any view of the case I find that the 
reference is not maintainable. 


The reference is accordingly rejected. 
Dictated and corrected by me. 


T. K. MUTSUDDI, 
Judge, 
28-] 2-68. 
T. K. MUTSUDDI, Judge, 
Fifth Industrial Tribunal. 
28-12-68.

Sarvashri Sourendra Mohan Moitra, Debendra-

Ch. Kundu? To what relief, if any, are they 
entitled ? 


As the Presiding Officer of the First Industrial Tri- 
bunal had not started work on that date, the said indus- 
trial dispute was withdrawn from the file of the First 
Industrial Tribunal and was transferred for disposal 
to this Tribunal by the Government of West Bengal, 
Labour Department, order No. 3103-1,R./IR/10L-87/67, 
dated the 10th July 1967, for adjudication in respect 
of the self-same issue as mentioned above. 


In pursuance of notices issued from this Tribunal the 
five workmen concerned and also the Company appear-

has been contended inter alia that the case of the work-

has no jurisdiction to entertain and adjudicate upon the
